summary: Andrew Getty, one of the heirs to billions of oil money, appears to have died of natural causes, a Los Angeles Police Department spokesman said. Andrew Getty, 47, had "several health issues," Aguilar said, adding that an autopsy will be conducted.

Jennifer Stewart's 2-year-old cat, Felix, remained missing nearly a week after an April 1 Etihad Airways flight from Abu Dhabi to New York, where the airline said he disappeared on Kennedy Airport grounds. Stewart believes he escaped because his carrier was badly damaged; Etihad is investigating, helping search for him with airport ground handlers and hired specialists, and plans to review its pet-handling procedures.

Shanghai, like many large Chinese cities, rations license plates as it looks for a solution to its gridlocked roads and polluted skies. Each month there are around 10,000 license plates available, and prospective car buyer Li Lifei said the final price at the most recent auction was 80,600 yuan ($13,000) -- around three times the price of a cheap Chinese car. Another option would be to buy a hybrid vehicle that automatically qualifies for a license plate, but Chinese drivers haven't wholeheartedly embraced the concept. For others, the hassles of buying and owning a car have become too much, and a recent report by consultants Bain & Company found that, of 2,137 people it surveyed, some 40% said cars were losing their appeal as a status symbol.

Only a few kilometers away, 147 people -- mostly students -- were brutally massacred when Al-Shabaab militants invaded the campus in Garissa, a town in northeastern Kenya. We've come to this particular Islamic religious school because the man suspected by Kenyan authorities of being the "mastermind" behind the atrocity -- Mohamed Mohamud -- once taught here. The Kenyan Interior Ministry has said at least one of the four gunmen who carried out the attack on the university was also Kenyan. The Kenyan government is concerned that Al-Shabaab is recruiting disaffected youth from inside the country.

Patrick Dempsey's character, Dr. Derek Shepherd, died after a car crash in Thursday night's "Grey's Anatomy," having first helped people involved in another accident. His departure came with a year remaining on Dempsey's contract and leaves Ellen Pompeo's Dr. Meredith Grey as the series' mainstay as its 11th season ends in May. Creator Shonda Rhimes said Shepherd would remain important to her, Meredith and the audience, and that his loss would affect everyone. Fans expressed shock and, in some cases, betrayal, while People published an obituary and #McDreamyForever trended on Twitter. The series will continue, with Pompeo contracted through season 12 and Rhimes having identified Meredith's ability to manage independently as this season's theme. For the week ending April 19, the show ranked 20th in total viewers and 12th among adults ages 18-49. Dempsey praised the show's global reach and devoted fans in comments to TVLine; he also has a development deal with ABC Studios, which produces the series.

Ebony Dickens of East Point, Georgia, posted her Facebook rant under the name Tiffany Milan, police said. The post called for shooting white police officers and said, "Might kill at least 15 tomorrow, I'm plotting now." East Point police said the posts "indicated that the acts were being plotted and were in motion." After connecting Dickens to the Facebook post, authorities obtained a search warrant for her residence and took her into custody while executing that warrant. "A firearm along with three computers was located during the search," East Point police said. Dickens, 33, appeared in court Wednesday on a charge of disseminating information related to terrorist acts. A judge set a $10,000 bond for her and banned her from social media. She was then transferred to Fulton County Jail, where she remained until bonding out at 6:19 a.m. Thursday, according to county sheriff's office spokeswoman Tracy Flanagan.
